chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: White musicians and pupils in Kansas City
summary: White musicians visited the black district, and she and Basie taught about thirty pupils, mostly white. Visiting whites played the Muehlebach Hotel.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did whites come down to the black clubs?

Yes, whites came everywhere; that's the reason why the guys got into trouble. They were always in the black district. Count Basie and I had about 30 pupils between us, that we were teaching to play jazz.
Did you have black pupils too?
Oh sure, we had both, but we had more whites than anything else.
Was there any jazz in the white sections of town in Kansas City?

There was jazz clubs. My attention was focused where the giants were and that was 18th and Vine or 12th Street. We had many white musicians that came there, mostly out of the city, like Ben Pollack and those people like that.
Oh, the Muhlenbach Hotel was a popular place for them there. I think that was the only one that they played.
